newsitem.title: USA: Online banking in U.S. seen growing rapidly.
newsitem.headline: Online banking in U.S. seen growing rapidly.

text.p: The number of online banking households in the U.S. is expected to grow 78 percent this year, Jupiter Communications said Wednesday.

Jupiter, a research group, projected more than 4.5 million online banking households by the end of 1997, compared with 2.5 million at the end of 1996. The number is expected to climb to 18 million households by the end of 2002, Jupiter said.
Scott Smith, director of Jupiter's digital commerce group, said many banks are turning to the Internet's World Wide Web of computer networks as the primary platform for online banking.

According to the Jupiter projections, the growth rate in new online banking households slows to 66 percent in 1998 and 34 percent in 1999. Jupiter said the market is expected to become saturated by 1999 as the pool of potential customers is mostly acquired and major players become established in the industry.
Jupiter said it believes monthly prices will gradually fall over the next six years, as an increasing number of banks offer free online banking.

Jupiter said that, as a result, cost savings rather than revenue generation will become the focus of the online banking market. It said the cost of an online banking transaction is estimated at less than one percent of the total cost of servicing a customer in a branch.
Chase Manhattan Corp, the largest U.S. bank and biggest in New York metropolitan area, announced free online banking this week. Citicorp has had it for some time.
